paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by hereditary nephritis progressing to end-stage renal disease, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and sensorineural deafness. Affected individuals lack the MER2 blood group antigen on their red cells.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) showed that CD151 carries the MER2 blood group antigen and is present on erythrocytes. It was the first member of the tetraspanin superfamily found on red cells. They examined the CD151 gene in 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin who had end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. All 3 patients were homozygous for a 1-nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151. The insertion caused a frameshift and a premature stop at codon 140, and was predicted to produce a truncated protein lacking the integrin-binding domain. The authors concluded that CD151 is essential for proper assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membranes in the kidney and is functionally significant in skin. They also suggested that CD151 is probably a component of the inner ear and could play a role in erythropoiesis.
